title: Would the updated forecast flip it?
hook: A toy action is attractive only when its expected net points exceed zero.

knows: basic arithmetic and how to compare two stated rules
doesNotKnow: how to show how a forecast update can change a decision while separating revision from demonstrated accuracy

misconception: Changing a probability estimate necessarily improves it, or cannot matter unless payoffs also change.
objective: Show how a forecast update can change a decision while separating revision from demonstrated accuracy.

claims.text: Original stipulated toy: Forecasts exogenous and hypothetical; no new evidence is generated; fixed signed net points; no Brier-score or forecast-improvement claim. Exact payoff inputs [{"label": "Forecast 20 percent", "values": [20, 10, -5]}, {"label": "Forecast 60 percent", "values": [60, 10, -5]}]; second author arithmetic check A=-2, B=4. At 20%, action averages {A}; at 60%, {B}. The changed probability crosses the positive-expectation threshold.

claims.text: Does it hold up? An updated probability is not automatically more accurate; forecast quality needs outcomes and scoring.
